docs.presetsFlips.component: The stock flip mechanics, each on its own page, drop-in. A flip is GEOMETRY (a reflection the
children inherit) plus, sometimes, CONTENT (the other face). `Atoms/Flippable` teaches the atom
through scenes; this shelf answers what each NAME already does, and how to configure it.
(the two deck modes), `directionFlip` (the readable row) and `contentSwap` (a recipe-maker the
consumer registers with their own subtree). A new one is a registration, never a branch anything
docs.presetsFlips.mirror: Pure geometry, nothing swapped — the default. Shown on a row of distinct tiles so the reflection is
visible: flip it and they come back in reverse screen order, mirrored about `axis`. The children
inherit the reflection through the chain; nothing walks the tree. `axis` is a parameter — 90 a
Y-mirror, 76 a 76° one — not a preset per angle.
docs.presetsFlips.turnover: The card: reflection AND the other face. Even `turns` is face-up — the front; odd shows the back
surface and mirrors. The two parities do it: reflection follows a node's own turns, the content swap
the summed. An empty back would fall through to the front, so a turn never blanks the card.
docs.presetsFlips.deckreorder: The deck turned as ONE PHYSICAL THING: the order reverses, the whole mirrors, every card shows its
back. The recipe only reorders — the cards' backs come from the SUMMED parity, each by its own
recipe, so no card is ever written to. Drop it on any container whose flip should reverse what is
on it; the distinct back tints here exist only so the reorder stays readable face-down.
docs.presetsFlips.deckchildren: The keep-order deck, the client2 alternative: cards turn in place, the order stays. As DATA this
recipe equals `mirror` — the chain turns the children on its own — but the name exists so a deck
can SAY its mode, put the two side by side, and swap one for the other without touching a node.
docs.presetsFlips.contentswap: The face that is a whole OTHER subtree. `contentSwap` is a recipe-MAKER: hand it the back as a
thunk and register the result under your own name — `registerFlip("ironBack", contentSwap(() =>
iron))` — and the atom only says `flip: "ironBack"`. References and config on the atom, the
mechanism in the registry. No reflection: a substitution is not a mirror, and the engine draws the
shown node's children, so the front never bleeds through.
docs.presetsFlips.directionflip: The readable row: the order reverses and NOTHING mirrors, so glyphs keep facing the reader — the
